takeaway: The rotator cuff is supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis; their tendons stabilise the head of the humerus in the glenohumeral joint.

question.text: The rotator cuff consists of the tendinous insertions of supraspinatus, infraspinatus and which other two muscles?

lines.text: Meet the rotator cuff team around the head of the humerus.
Supraspinatus sits on top, and infraspinatus is behind.
Together their tendons surround the head anteriorly, posteriorly and superiorly.
The other two heroes are teres minor and subscapularis.
Teres major, deltoid and rhomboid minor are not part of the cuff, so they sit on the bench.
lines.say: (laugh) Teres major, deltoid and rhomboid minor are not part of the cuff, so they sit on the bench.

lines.text: A strong cuff keeps the humeral head stable under the acromion.
When it is deficient, the head migrates up and impinges, with weak abduction.
